page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c1.large is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine instance within the ecs.c1 server family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio aligns the instance with compute-focused workloads. The instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a hardware capability perspective, the underlying CPU architecture lacks support for advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and hardware-accelerated cryptography (AES, SHA). This absence of specialized vector and matrix instruction sets limits its efficiency for modern machine learning inference, heavy cryptography, or advanced signal processing. However, the dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities without resource contention, offering a predictable compute profile for standard integer-based processing tasks.

Given the compute-oriented resource distribution and the lack of local storage, the ecs.c1.large is structured for workloads that rely on external network storage and require dedicated CPU cycles. Appropriate applications include web serving, distributed compute nodes, batch processing, and lightweight application servers that do not require specialized hardware acceleration or high memory-per-core ratios.
